answer: A retired carbon credit anchors one identity to one verified project, because a registry like Verra issues it only after a third-party audit of real emission cuts and a public retirement record. Three established peers check the credit serial numbers in the registry, the auditor's report, and a fresh signature before the agent can answer. Each fake pays $10,000 to $50,000 for its own audit and credits, so an opal field of fakes needs a thousand projects and $10 million, like an ivory tower that only holds one project at a time, and a cipher of fake identities still pays for every audit.
